issue.title: S1.5 · Rate-limit resend requests per device
issue.body:
### Summary
A device that keeps asking for the same file makes the sender upload it again and again, up to 200 MB each time (T-D3). It floods the room's relay and the sender's data.

### Acceptance (the attack fails)
- Per device and per file, whole-file sends are allowed at most 3 times in any 60 seconds. A whole-file send is a `want`, a `need` with no list of pieces, or a `need` whose list covers more than half the file's pieces. Requests over the limit are dropped and nothing is sent.
- Requests for a few missing pieces (a `need` listing half the pieces or fewer) are allowed at most once a second per device per file. The receiver's own retries are 1.5–3 s apart, so they're never dropped.
- Dropped requests don't count towards the limit, so a device can't keep itself locked out.
- Requests for a file this device doesn't have are dropped before they're counted.
- The counters are bounded: they're cleared when a device leaves and capped in number. The limits are named constants in `LIMITS` (Rule 3).

### Edge cases
- A real transfer that loses pieces on the relay still finishes: its retries stay under the limit.
- The limit is per device: a second device asking for the same file still gets it.
- After 60 seconds the same device can ask again.

### Must not break
- `npm run test:browsers`, direct and relay: every check still passes, including the late guest's download and the silent-device timeout.

### How to test the attack
In the two-browser test, B sends A 20 `want` messages for the same photo within a second, then 20 `need` messages listing every piece within a second. Each time A sends the file at most 3 times (count A's outgoing sends for that photo). A third device then asks once and still gets the file.
